subject: Priority availability exception request — Borealis Health
messages:
From: Clara Shaw <c.shaw@borealishealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Priority availability for Q3 rollout

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the kickoff last week. We need to lock an availability and operational support commitment for our HCP-facing inference traffic ahead of our Q3 product launch (target date 2027-08-15). The ask from the product/ops side is:

- Target p95 latency <= 120ms for text-generation endpoints at our expected traffic profile (steady-state ~300 reqs/s, peak ~650 reqs/s).
- 99.9% availability SLA on the production route for the first 90 days.
- Dedicated warm capacity (reserved pool) during launch week and a 4-week on-call war room with an SRE liaison.

We understand this is an exception to standard tiers and are prepared to discuss committed spend. Please share a feasibility note, estimated incremental costs, and what operational guarantees you can provide (runbook, paging rotations, monitoring retention). Attached is our integration plan and traffic profile.

Clara Shaw
Head of Integrations, Borealis Health
c.shaw@borealishealth.com

Attachments: borealis-maplans-v3.pdf

- Feasible from an ops/runtime perspective? (Monica)

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Priority availability for Q3 rollout

Quick read and commercial thoughts:

- Feels doable if we provision a dedicated reserved pool sized for peak (650 reqs/s) with a 20% buffer. That will avoid noisy-neighbor variance and reduce cold-start exposure.
- Proposed commercial structure:
  - Reserved capacity commitment (3 months) — baseline monthly commit + uplift for the buffer.
  - One-time onboarding fee to cover runbook creation, playbook drills, and 24/7 war room staffing for the 4-week launch window.
  - Optional premium support add-on for longer retention of fine-grained traces.

Ballpark numbers (internal only): additional ~$48k/month for reserved capacity + one-time ~$12k onboarding. Exact numbers depend on model family (we should pin model variants) and quantization profile.

Action items for ops/product: need confirmation on exact SLO semantics (is 99.9% applied to route-level p95 or to availability) and acceptance criteria for the 4-week war room. Also need an SRE-run runbook.

Karthik
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.ngwood@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Priority availability for Q3 rollout

Operational feasibility notes (high level):

- We can meet p95 <= 120ms for text-gen at the traffic profile if we:
  1) Reserve a warm pool of GPUs colocated in the US region with pinned model versions and fixed batch sizing.
  2) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for common prompt prefixes they mentioned in the integration plan.
  3) Maintain a hot standby pool and an automated failover route to the standby region.

- Risks / open items:
  - Cold-starts for infrequent routes could spike p95; mitigation is routing + warming.
  - p95 vs availability: need to be explicit. We recommend defining SLA as \"99.9% route availability with p95 objective of <= 120ms under steady-state traffic\" and include an exclusion for traffic spikes above the agreed profile.
  - Monitoring: we will need 90-day retention for per-request traces during the launch window (adds storage cost).

- Deliverables required before committing:
  - Ops runbook (attached draft) with escalation matrix and rollback thresholds.
  - Load profile confirmation from Borealis.
  - A staged rollout plan: canary -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% over 3 days, with rollbacks defined.

I attached a draft runbook for review (priority-runbook-draft.pdf). Once product signs off on the SLA language, we can size the pool and produce a cost estimate for Karthik to include in the commercial offer.

Monica Patel
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachments: priority-runbook-draft.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: Priority availability for Q3 rollout

Thanks everyone — pragmatic thread. I support approving an exception for Borealis Health conditioned on the following:

1) Product (Stephanie) to finalize SLA wording that includes the explicit traffic profile, exclusion clauses, and rollback triggers.
2) Ops (Monica) to sign off on the runbook and the staged rollout cadence.
3) Sales (Karthik) to include the 3-month reserved commitment and onboarding fee in the term sheet and obtain PO/DocuSign acceptance before provisioning.
4) Exec sponsor confirmation (I will be the exec sponsor for the exception).

Michael — please consolidate the items above and send a short mutual action plan to Clara with attachments and a DocuSign link. Copy Stephanie for legal guards and Monica for runbook sign-off. Once we have the signed DocuSign, ops will provision the reserved pool within 48 hours.

Marcus Lin
VP, Product Operations — Redwood Inference
